newsitem.title: SPAIN: MOTOR RACING-MANSELL REVELS IN RETURN TO FORMULA ONE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-MANSELL REVELS IN RETURN TO FORMULA ONE.

text.p: Nigel Mansell may have lost his famous moustache but he proved he had mislaid none of his equally-famed commitment at the Circuit de Catalunya on Wednesday when he began a two-day test with the Jordan team.

Revelling in the buzz of being alongside the top Formula One teams, including Williams, Ferrari, McLaren and Benetton at a serious winter test, the 1992 world drivers' champion completed 49 laps to clock a best time of one minute 22.89 seconds.
His Jordan team mate Ralf Schumacher, younger brother of former world champion Michael Schumacher, had done 3,000 kilometres of testing and recorded a best of 1:22.59.

Mansell's time was not enough to push him up among the fastest runners, led by Canadian Jacques Villeneuve in a Williams, but it proved he retained the skill and desire to compete among the best combinations in the sport.

"He surprised me with his commitment," admitted team boss Eddie Jordan, of the 43-year-old veteran who is flirting with a serious racing return to the sport after more than 18 months out of the cockpit.

"After three laps I could see he was commiting himself and it was fantastic to see it. He is a guy who has always had fantastic belief in himself, in his own talents and a lot of the other younger guys around could learn from that."

Mansell, who paid his own expeneses to be at the test, said it was being treated by both him and the Jordan team as a "bit of fun" but he admitted he enjoyed the experience of being re-acquainted with an F1 car.
"I think the really nice thing is that there is no pressure from either side on the other and that is the way I like it," said Mansell.

The 1992 world champion said there was a 60/40 chance that he would be racing next year in Formula One or Indycars, although that could be affected by problems in the U.S. where he has contractual restrictions in place to the end of 1997.
Asked after the test when a decision on his future with Jordan would be made, he laughed and passed it to Jordan. The team chief said: "It takes two to tango..."
Jordan revealed that he had offered Mansell the drive as a bit of fun during a round of golf and the former world champion had found it irresistible.

Mansell denied he felt he had unfinished business in Formula One after his exit from McLaren, where in 1995 he endured two desultory races before walking away, but confessed there was a great deal of attraction in the prospect of helping Jordan develop into a winning team.
"We didn't retire," he said. "We stood down."

"Racing has been in my blood for 20 years. You have either got it or you haven't and it is not something you lose easily. I have kept myself fit by playing a lot of golf and lowering my handicap to just one -- and having three children keeps you going, too.
Both Jordan and Mansell used their post-test news conference as a chance to share some knockabout humour during which Jordan made it clear he had not made Mansell any financial offers.
Asked if he was prepared to break the bank to sign him, Jordan said: "Well, you go into these things with a degree of reality -- but he (Mansell) has one sense of reality...and I have another."
